method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Quantity table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

Use your checked Week 1 plan. The adult gives GO before ingredients or tools are issued. Follow the actual approved quantities and any agreed substitution.
Original invented teaching pictures. Read left to right: prepare, mix, assemble. These are not pupil work or an exact guide to quantities.
After the adult’s checks, wash hands with soap and water and dry them. Wash the carrot, cabbage and apple. Grate the carrot and finely slice the cabbage with adult-approved tools and supervision. Use prepared vegetables if agreed.
Mash 80 g of cooked beans labelled ready to eat with a fork. Mix in about 20 g from the single 60 g yoghurt portion. Add the carrot and cabbage. An adult opens tins and removes sharp lids.
Put the filling on the wholemeal wrap and fold it. Serve with the apple and the remaining yoghurt. Ask the adult to check the plate and store or serve it safely. Tasting is optional.

Use these prompts with the adult. A tick follows an actual check or action. A blank check does not mean it is safe to continue.
[ ] Adult clears the private allergy and dietary checks from current school records and actual ingredient labels.
[ ] Wash and dry hands. Clean the surface and tools. Tie hair back and cover cuts.
[ ] Use the checked plan, agreed tools and cooked ready-to-eat beans. Keep chilled food refrigerated until needed.
[ ] Use only approved tools with the agreed supervision. Put a tool down before asking for help.
[ ] Keep food and utensils protected from raw-food contamination and allergen cross-contact. Use clean utensils and do not share tasting spoons.
[ ] If there is a spill, a cut, an unexpected ingredient or uncertainty, stop and tell the adult. Keep chilled food out for the shortest preparation time.
[ ] Adult agrees immediate serving, refrigeration at 0–5°C, or disposal. Follow use-by and storage instructions.
[ ] Adult transfers unused beans from an opened tin into a clean covered food container before refrigeration.
[ ] Clear and clean using the agreed routine. Put waste away, wash hands and complete the actual record.
In your book: one action before ___. One action during ___. One action after ___. Help used ___. Anything unfinished or changed ___.
GO depends on the adult’s checks from records, actual ingredients and facilities. Stop for uncertainty. Tasting is optional.

The planned meal is already a no-heat dish. This route removes pupil knife and grater use by supplying prepared vegetables.
Approve the actual food, individual records, labels, hygiene facilities, clean equipment and cold storage. A room without a kitchen still needs potable handwashing water, suitable cleaning and a food-safe work surface. A checked cold container must maintain 0–5°C. If any condition fails, use simulation.
Use the pupil’s checked bean and vegetable wrap plan. An adult supplies washed, pre-cut vegetables, washed fruit and cooked ready-to-eat beans. Use a fork, bowl and clean surface. Keep the same approved ingredient amounts.
1 Prepare the clean station and wash and dry hands. Use the adult-prepared produce.
2 Mash the beans. Mix in about 20 g from the single 60 g yoghurt portion and add the vegetables.
3 Fill and fold the wrap. Serve fruit and remaining yoghurt. Follow the adult’s storage and cleaning decision.
With no safe food facilities, food or equipment, rehearse with empty hands or pictures. The pupil explains or directs the three steps and names a safety action at each point. Record this as planning or simulation, not preparation. Mark the practical and any plate photo pending. Rebook the practical when the adult can meet all safety requirements.
In your book: cold assembly / simulation ___. Actions I completed ___. Adult actions ___. Safe checks observed ___. Plate photo actual location / pending ___. No tasting or photo is invented.

Use only a photograph of the pupil’s actual food. The recipe pictures are teaching models and must never be submitted as pupil evidence.
The adult uses an approved device after food handling stops. Place the food on a plain surface. Keep all people, faces, hands, names, labels, screens and reflections out of the frame. Keep the device away from food preparation.
Use the approved private storage process. Prevent automatic upload or public posting. Before export or attachment, the adult verifies a copy with location and other identifying metadata removed. Restore hand hygiene before returning to food handling.

Metadata check completed ___. Food-only frame checked ___. No public or automatic upload confirmed ___. Support used ___.
I prepared ___ with ___ help. One safe action I used was ___. One real change was ___.
Mark the photo pending. Keep a truthful drawing or written plate description with the adult’s observations of preparation. Label the record as a drawing or description. It is not a photo. Record what actually happened and arrange a suitable photo opportunity only if appropriate.
A photograph shows the plate. It does not prove safe preparation or independent tool use. Keep process observations alongside it. Do not include completed private records in public teaching files.

Weekly outcome verbatim: FOODWISE: prepare a 2-3 step dish safely.
I can follow my checked plan to prepare a simple dish and show safe working.
[ ] I can complete the agreed preparation steps with the support I need.
[ ] I can show hygiene and safe tool use before, during and after making.
[ ] I can keep an honest record of my finished plate and the support used.
Prepare the washed produce using agreed tools or adult-prepared vegetables. Mash ready-to-eat beans and mix the filling. Fill and fold the wrap and serve the sides.
If a label, ingredient, tool or support need changes, stop and ask the adult to check it. A familiar package is not permission to use it.
Keep a record of the actual dish, safety actions, support and real changes. Record a food-only plate photo privately, or leave photo status pending. A teaching picture or simulation does not prove preparation.
A useful adjustment keeps the meal possible and safe. Ask for help, prepared ingredients or another approved route when needed.
In your book. Rehearse in any language. No tasting is compulsory. Share personal health information privately with the adult.
